status_summary: The 2026 National Defense Strategy (posted 2026-01-23) keeps a one-war-plus planning model, according to CSIS: the United States plans for one major war, with a second conflict, such as defending Europe against Russia while fighting China, handled largely by allies. CSIS says the strategy acknowledges the simultaneity problem but gives no force size, structure or posture figures, and a Reagan Institute analysis reads it as conceding that the United States cannot plan to fight two major wars at once. No service-by-service two-war scenarios were found in public descriptions.

timeline.event: The Department of War released the 2026 National Defense Strategy, which per CSIS keeps a one-war-plus construct with a second conflict falling largely to allies and gives no force-size figures.

The House passes H.R. 8800, the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act, 216 to 212; sections 130 and 255 would require torpedo and sonobuoy inventory strategies sufficient for two simultaneous regional conflicts, with no general force-sizing construct.

title: Adopt a two-war force-sizing construct with scenarios for each service
uncertainties: The strategy text could not be fetched in this review (the hosting site blocks the research tools); its source entry is copied from c04-08, which read it through a browser retrieval, and the posting date comes from the hosting address. Descriptions of the force-sizing construct come from CSIS (dated 2026-01-27) and the Reagan Institute (dated 2026-07-01), which agree that the strategy does not plan for two simultaneous wars; a Stimson Center analysis, whose page prints no date and is marked undated, says the strategy admits the United States cannot manage concurrent conflicts alone. Diverged is chosen because the stated construct is materially different from a two-war standard; not_started is an alternative if the strategy's silence on force sizing is read as no decision. The classified force-planning guidance is not public. Public Law 119-60 Sec. 364 (report on critical munitions for simultaneous conflicts) was seen only as a title. Checked systematically on 2026-10-18: Federal Register queries of Defense Department documents, the Unified Agenda landing page (not applicable to a strategy document), a congress.gov and GovInfo search with BILLSTATUS reads, Defense Department pages (blocked or unfetched), and one news search found no adoption of a two-war construct. H.R. 8800, the FY2027 defense authorization bill, passed the House 216 to 212 on 2026-07-22 and was received in the Senate on 2026-09-14; sections 130 and 255 direct torpedo and sonobuoy strategies sized to inventories for not fewer than two simultaneous regional conflicts. These are munitions-inventory planning assumptions in an unenacted bill, not a force-sizing construct or service scenarios, so the stage is unchanged; proposed 5 with a partial match is the other defensible call if a House-passed two-conflict sufficiency standard is read as a step toward the construct. The Senate bill (S. 4784) had a motion to proceed on 2026-07-27 and has not passed. The GovInfo engrossed text could be read only through section 133.
